text:
Situation: Gentamicin sulfate has been on FDA's shortage list since 2021-07-23 and remains listed as of 2026-10-21, a duration of 63 months. Current inventory shows Corvale East at 9 days on hand for the 40 mg/mL 2 mL vial, Corvale General at 17 days, and Corvale Lakeside at 19 days. Corvale East also holds a separate 40 mg/mL 2 mL vial lot with only 2 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): FDA posted the shortage on 2021-07-23. Earlier inspections of the same plant received OAI classifications ending 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04. An alternate manufacturer, Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC, is not on FDA's shortage list today; its plant last received a VAI classification on 2023-08-24.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on the primary injectable presentation. Internal transfers can provide immediate but limited relief. Procurement from Fresenius Kabi offers a supply source not currently in shortage. Alternate manufacturers Hospira and Hikma have approved substitutions available.

Recommended actions:
1. Execute transfer of 41 units from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Execute transfer of 140 units from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Place purchase order with Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC — approved by buyer.
4. Activate Hospira, Inc. substitution for GENTAMICIN SULFATE 40 mg/mL — approved by pharmacist.
5. Activate Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. substitution for Gentamicin 40 mg/mL — approved by pharmacist.

Not recommended: Delaying transfers or purchases pending further FDA updates; the shortage has persisted 63 months without resolution.
